title: Dose-Fractionated Spectrum Imaging for the Analysis of Organic and Inorganic Interfaces
content: Electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) in the scanning transmission electron microscope (S)TEM has the advantage of acquiring compositional data from materials at the nanometer and sub-nanometer length scales. Due to the relatively small cross-sections of the ionization edges acquired with EELS, the dose to achieve these high resolutions ranges from 106 to 108 e-/Å2. Many material systems that EELS has been traditionally applied to can tolerate these relatively high doses. However, soft materials such as polymers and organic materials often have a lower dose tolerance of 4 – 6 orders of magnitude lower than metals, semiconductors, and some oxides. This requires the dose to be spread over larger areas to maintain sample integrity, which limits spatial resolution.
